facts.text: The environment simulates the movements of multiple robots in an environment with barriers and a target, and the goal is to navigate the robots to the target while avoiding collisions
The action space is a Dict of two Box arrays named vR and vL, each with one value per robot and each element bounded by -max_velocity and +max_velocity
The observation is a Dict with vR, vL and theta (one value per robot), robot_positions (n_robots x 2), future_target_position (2) and future_obstacle_positions ((n_barriers - 1) x 2)
The play field corners are x from -4.0 to 4.0 and y from -3.0 to 3.0
A reset draws each barrier position uniformly between the play-field bounds and each barrier velocity from a normal distribution with standard deviation barrier_velocity_range
A reset draws the target index uniformly from 0 to n_barriers - 1
A reset places robot i at x = left play-field corner - 0.5, y = -2.0 + 0.8 * i, with theta 0.0
Barriers move by their velocity times dt on every step, and a velocity component is reversed when the barrier passes the matching play-field edge
The wheel spacing of the differential-drive model is twice robot_radius
The pose model moves straight when the wheel speeds are equal, rotates in place when they are opposite, and follows an arc otherwise
A step limits each wheel's speed change to max_acceleration * dt, then integrates the pose over dt
The future obstacle and target positions are predicted by advancing a copy of the barriers steps_ahead_to_plan steps without moving the simulation state

A robot closer than barrier_radius + robot_radius to the target barrier earns reach_target_reward and a new target is drawn; the same distance to another barrier or another robot earns collision_penalty
An episode is terminated only when reset_when_target_reached is true and a robot reached the target; truncated is always false
The info dictionary reports n_robots, max_acceleration, max_velocity, barrier_radius, robot_radius, dt and tau
The environment is registered as PlanningMultiRobot-v0 with entry point planning_multi_robot_gym:PlanningMultiRobotEnv
The environment metadata declares the render modes rgb_array and human with render_fps 30

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 fixes the initial state and the dynamics are deterministic, so one implementation repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions; this package's fake draws the initial state with Python's random.Random and upstream with numpy's generator, so a seed gives different trajectories on the two

gaps: planar differential-drive kinematics of circular robots: no body geometry beyond a radius, no wheel slip, friction, actuator dynamics, sensor model or noise; collisions are distance tests between circles, and the target and the barriers move as point-like circles
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms only
no physical device is modelled and the model was never validated against one

the fake backend re-implements the environment with Python floats and random.Random and was not compared with the upstream environment (the upstream package is not installed and gymnasium/pygame are absent where the gate runs): trajectories differ from upstream's numpy random stream and array dtypes
the info member predict_position is a Python callable and is omitted from the JSON state
no rendering: the fake reports render_mode None and returns no frame; cap.world.render.v1 stays unbound
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state or set_state

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
